scenes.en: What really happens in a complete eye test?
scenes.say: What really happens in a complete eye test? If you have never had one, or it has been years since your last check, this video walks you through every step, so you know exactly what to expect.

scenes.en: Many eye problems start without any pain
scenes.ta: பல கண் பிரச்சனைகள் வலி இல்லாமல் தொடங்கும்
scenes.say: First, why get your eyes tested at all? Many eye problems start slowly and without any pain. You may simply get used to slightly blurred vision, or think your headaches are from work stress. A regular eye test catches these changes early.

scenes.en: A short chat about your eyes and health
scenes.ta: உங்கள் கண் மற்றும் உடல்நலம் பற்றி கேட்போம்
scenes.say: Step one is a short conversation. The optometrist asks about any blur, headaches, eye strain or watering, how much screen time you have, what work you do, and whether you have diabetes or high blood pressure. Family history matters too, so mention if a parent has glaucoma or wears thick glasses.

scenes.en: Reading the letter chart, one eye at a time
scenes.say: Step two is the familiar letter chart. You cover one eye and read the smallest line you can, then switch eyes. This measures your distance vision. For small children who cannot read yet, picture or symbol charts are used instead.

scenes.en: A quick machine reading of your eye power
scenes.say: Step three is often a computerised reading. You look into a machine at a picture, and in a few seconds it gives a starting estimate of your eye power. It is quick and painless, but it is only a starting point, not the final prescription.

scenes.en: Fine-tuning with lenses: is 1 or 2 clearer?
scenes.ta: லென்ஸ் மாற்றி: ஒன்றா இரண்டா, எது தெளிவு?
scenes.say: Step four is the most important part. The optometrist places different lenses in front of your eyes and asks, which is clearer, one or two? There are no wrong answers. Just say what you see. If both look the same, say that too. This fine-tuning gives you a prescription that is comfortable, not just sharp.

scenes.en: Checking your near vision for reading and phone
scenes.say: Step five checks your near vision, the distance you use for reading and your phone. After the age of about forty, most people find close work harder. This is natural, and it is why reading glasses or progressive lenses are often needed.

scenes.en: How well both eyes work together
scenes.say: Step six looks at how well both eyes work together as a team, how they move and focus. This is especially important for children, because a squint or a lazy eye is best treated early.

scenes.en: A look at eye health, and referral if needed
scenes.say: Step seven is a look at the health of the eye. Depending on your age and history, further checks such as eye pressure or a retina examination may be advised. If anything needs medical attention, you will be referred to an eye specialist.

Now, your prescription. S P H, or sphere, is your main power. Minus means short sight, plus means long sight. C Y L, or cylinder, corrects astigmatism, and the axis tells the direction of that correction.

scenes.en: ADD is extra power for reading
scenes.say: If you see A D D, that is extra power added for reading and close work. It usually appears after forty, and it is the power used in bifocal and progressive lenses.

scenes.en: Bring your old glasses and contact lenses
scenes.say: A few tips before your test. Bring your current glasses or contact lens details. If you wear contact lenses, ask whether to remove them before the test. And tell the optometrist about any health conditions.

scenes.en: Children: every year. Adults: every 1 to 2 years.
scenes.say: How often should you get tested? Children, once a year, especially once they start school. Adults, every one to two years. And if you have diabetes, get a retina check every year, even if your vision feels fine.

scenes.en: Sudden blur, pain or flashes? See an eye specialist now.
scenes.ta: திடீர் பார்வை மங்கல் அல்லது வலி? உடனே மருத்துவரை பாருங்கள்
scenes.say: Do not wait for your routine check if you notice sudden blurred vision, eye pain, redness that does not settle, or flashes of light. See an eye specialist straight away.
